drivers.variant_notes: Production CPU set with VSU-100 U9 speech ROM.

Hardware compatibility for the documented replay-knocker setup requires moving the former coin-lockout lead at A3J2-8 (public 18) to the knocker. Keep the walker at A3J5-12 (public 9) and the stock VSU-100 U9 speech ROM. The DIP 14 routing selection is documented from subversion 39 onward. In 3335, DIP 18 selects a countdown reset, DIP 19 selects free play and DIP 23 selects a center-Special extra ball. The revised switch test cycles closed contacts. Author documentation [release.flight-2000.idleman-v33]. Retained runtime traces cover flight2k and flightfp.

Hardware compatibility requires the revised VSU-100 speech ROMs and wiring that matches DIP 14. With DIP 14 ON, keep the walker at A3J5-12 (public 9) and move the former coin-lockout lead at A3J2-8 (public 18) to the replay knocker. With DIP 14 OFF, swap those leads so A3J2-8 (public 18) drives the walker and A3J5-12 (public 9) drives the knocker. The author allows omitting the knocker on the unswapped harness with DIP 14 ON. A DIP/wiring mismatch can damage the driver board. PinMAME loads two revised 2716 speech images at U9 and U10. The author also documents one 2532 at U9 with U10 empty on physical hardware. DIP 17 selects attract speech, DIP 19 selects free play and DIP 23 selects a center-Special extra ball. Adjustments 19–22 set tilt warnings, high-score replays, maximum credits and multiball difficulty. Author documentation [release.flight-2000.idleman-3347m]. Retained runtime traces cover flight2k and flightfp.
Always-free-play U5 and U6 replacements use the production U1, U2 and VSU-100 U9. The stock all-DIPs-off boot test is retained.

physical.notes: Bank 3 bit 6. On flight2k and flightfp this bit participates in the all-DIPs-off boot test and has no individual gameplay option. On flight2m and flight2mb, ON makes the center Special award an extra ball. OFF uses DIP 31/32, which also select the outlane award in either setting.

mechanisms.behavior: The common reset raises all five targets. Five individual actuators trip targets down to spot the lit countdown target. The controller follows each leaf switch when its target is down.
mechanisms.label: Left five-target memory bank

mechanisms.behavior: Hitting the three targets closes their individual contacts. A single reset raises the bank. Completing the bank advances the multiplier and right spinner value.
mechanisms.label: Right three-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: One coil retracts a common bar, moving alternate pivoted fingers in the covered lane. The spring brings the entry finger fully up between strokes. Switch 39 closes on arrival and clears once the ball parks past the wireform. Two balls can remain staged between fingers. When qualified, the next ball initiates staged release via the left and right kickouts. Switch 40 is the separate release rollover used after qualification. With 35 open, the 65-second stock boot probe observed repeated right kickout, left kickout and walker commands with no coin or Start input. A bowed bar can trap the first finger halfway, causing an incoming ball to overshoot and eject back down the entrance.
mechanisms.label: Ball walker and launcher

mechanisms.behavior: The first stage holds the ball at the left kickout contact and propels it toward the next stage when the ROM drives the left kicker.
mechanisms.label: First-stage Apollo kickout

mechanisms.behavior: The second stage holds the ball at the right kickout contact and propels it toward the upper arch when the ROM drives the right kicker.
mechanisms.label: Second-stage Apollo kickout

mechanisms.behavior: The three switches report ball occupancy under the apron. With all three closed at power-up the stock ROM skips the recovery cycle. A common kicker serves one ball toward the shooter lane. Release the appropriate occupancy contact as the stack settles after each real serve. Surviving units show the shared feed effect with above-wood and below-wood serve actuator mountings.
mechanisms.label: Three-position out-hole and shooter feed
